patch.objective: Creating and managing short-lived service account credentials

sources.cite: Google Cloud, Associate Cloud Engineer certification exam guide: setting up (~20%), planning and configuring (~17.5%), deploying and implementing (~25%), ensuring successful operation (~20%), configuring access and security (~17.5%)
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Bullets quoted: 4.5 'Working with Cloud DNS and Cloud NAT'; 3.5 'Creating ingress and egress firewall rules and policies'; 3.5 'Peering external networks (e.g., Cloud VPN, VPC Network Peering)'. The page shows five sections where the course seed has four units, and does not mention CMEK or Query Insights, which the seed's objectives do: a difference for the verification pass (finding in docs/sims.md 22.39).

sources.cite: Google Cloud documentation, IAM: Delete and undelete service accounts
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Relevant text: deleting a service account immediately cuts off applications that use it; a new account with the same name is a separate identity that does not inherit the old one's roles; undelete works for 30 days; 'If you're unsure whether anything still uses an account, Google recommends disabling it instead of deleting it.' Disabling a single key (gcloud iam service-accounts keys disable) and the audit log fields are from memory of the key management pages (to verify).
